name: set_thread_area
synopsis: Note: glibc provides no wrappers for these system calls, necessitating the use of syscall(2).
description: set_thread_area() provides architecture-specific support for thread-local storage, allowing the storage of a pointer or setting of a TLS entry in the GDT on supported architectures like x86, m68k, MIPS, and C-SKY. It is primarily used by threading libraries to manage thread-specific data.

parameters.name: u_info
parameters.description: Pointer to a user_desc structure containing TLS entry details (on x86); varies by architecture, e.g., unsigned long tp on m68k

return_value.success: Returns 0 on success (always on C-SKY, MIPS, m68k; on x86 for set_thread_area)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error (on x86), with errno set to indicate the error

errors.description: get_thread_area() or set_thread_area() was invoked as a 64-bit system call
A free TLS entry could not be located

bugs: On 64-bit kernels before Linux 3.19, certain padding bits in user_desc could prevent a TLS entry from being cleared properly; prior to Linux 3.19, DS and ES segment registers must not reference TLS entries.
